entities.name: Jerusalem Talmud (Yerushalmi)
entities.label: Text
entities.summary: The earlier of the two Talmuds, compiled in the rabbinic academies of Roman Palestine (Tiberias, Caesarea, Sepphoris) around 350–400 CE. Shorter and more concise than the Babylonian Talmud, the Yerushalmi covers 39 of the Mishnah's 63 tractates with particular strength in agricultural laws (relevant to the Land of Israel) and provides invaluable historical information about Jewish life under Roman rule. While ultimately overshadowed in legal authority by the Bavli, the Jerusalem Talmud preserves distinct Palestinian traditions, variant legal opinions, and historical data unavailable elsewhere.
